sections.h2: How does selling a house in Bethlehem work?
sections.html:
A Bethlehem sale runs through an agreement of sale, a city housing inspection, settlement and a recorded deed, and the city inspection is the step that surprises most sellers. Your parcel may sit in Northampton County or, on the West Side, in Lehigh County, and that choice decides which recorder of deeds and which assessment office you deal with. Confirm the county before you list.

The city is a different jurisdiction from Bethlehem Township, which runs its own resale program. A house inside the city limits answers to the city's rules described below.

sections.h2: Who lives in Bethlehem and who buys there?
sections.html:
Bethlehem is a Lehigh River city of roughly 79,600 people with 19.12 square miles of land area, and its housing and buyer pool reflect its mix of old neighborhoods, college campuses and former industrial ground. The Census Bureau counted 75,781 residents in April 2020 and estimated 79,644 for July 2025, a gain of 5.1 percent.

Moravian settlers named the town on Christmas Eve 1741, and the city now has five areas: Center City, the West Side, the East Side, the South Side and the North Side. Only the West Side lies in Lehigh County. Bethlehem Steel stopped metal production at its Bethlehem plant in 1995, and the site now holds the Wind Creek casino and the SteelStacks arts campus. Lehigh University, Moravian University, St. Luke's hospital in neighboring Fountain Hill, B. Braun and Guardian Life are among the larger employers named in the city's history. Public schools belong to the Bethlehem Area School District.

sections.h2: What do the housing numbers say about Bethlehem?
sections.html:
Bethlehem is close to an even split between owners and renters, and the typical owned home is valued at $260,400. The American Community Survey figures that Census QuickFacts reports for 2020 through 2024 are:

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 49.9 percent.
  • Typical home value among owners: $260,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,382 a month.
  • Households: 31,052, averaging 2.30 people.
  • Median household income: $68,879, with a mean commute of 22.1 minutes.

Because about half of households rent, a good share of the houses that change hands in the city have been rentals at some point. That makes the rental license rules further down relevant to many sellers.

sections.h2: Does Bethlehem inspect a house before it sells?
sections.html:
Yes. Under Article 119 of the city's codified ordinances, every transferor of real property must have the city's Housing Inspections Bureau inspect it before title passes, and the city page confirms the rule covers residential and commercial property alike. The inspection checks the house against the International Property Maintenance Code and the uses the zoning ordinance allows.

The requirement was amended by Ordinance 2026-19, passed on July 21, 2026. The table summarizes what the current text of section 119.04 says.

ItemWhat the city ordinance provides
When to callWithin 10 days of offering the property for sale
Lead timeBook the inspection a month or more ahead of the transfer
ReportLists uncorrected housing, building, safety or fire violations, plus zoning classification and legality of use
Who gets itGiven to the buyer and attached to the agreement of sale, with any notice of assessment for public improvements
Buyer's dutyBuyer must still obtain a certificate of occupancy
Penalty (section 119.99)Fine of $600 or up to 90 days in jail, or both

Source: City of Bethlehem, Article 119 and the Housing Inspections page. The bureau takes scheduling calls Monday through Friday at (610) 865-7091 or (610) 865-7097.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Bethlehem house?
sections.html:
The right route depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close, and the city inspection applies to all of them. Each route carries the same obligation to schedule the inspection and hand the report to the buyer.

  • List with an agent: the widest buyer pool, with showings, repairs ahead of the inspection and a closing date set by the buyer's financing.
  • Sell it yourself: you keep the agent's fee in your pocket but handle the agreement of sale, the city report and the disclosures on your own.
  • Take a cash offer: buyers who pay cash usually buy as is and close on a date you agree, which suits a house with open violations, tenants or deferred repairs. The violations report still goes to that buyer.

Compare offers on the net you keep after repairs, taxes and any city-required fixes, not only on the headline price.

sections.h2: What should a landlord selling a Bethlehem rental know?
sections.html:
Every residential rental unit in Bethlehem must be licensed each year, and Article 1738 puts rental units on an inspection cycle of once every three years. A landlord who sells should know where the license stands before listing.

Rooming houses need an annual inspection under Article 1735, and properties occupied by students or unrelated people fall under Article 1739. When a tenant lives in the house, plan the sale inspection around their access and notice rights, and ask the Housing Inspections Bureau whether your license is current before you list.

sections.h2: Which taxes and fees come out of a Bethlehem sale?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent realty transfer tax on the value transferred, and the grantor and grantee are jointly liable for it. Recording offices collect it at the same time as any local transfer tax.

The city's own tax is set in Article 335. It names a 1 percent rate and then cuts the city's share to one half whenever another taxing body also levies the tax on the same transfer, so the combined local rate on a Bethlehem deed depends on how the city and the school district divide it. The Recorder of Deeds in Lehigh or Northampton County collects the local tax and passes it to the city less a 2 percent commission. Ask the recorder for the total on your deed. Transfers between certain close relatives and property passing by succession are excluded, per the state Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: Who handles recording and assessment in Bethlehem?
sections.html:
The recorder of deeds for Northampton County or Lehigh County records the deed, depending on where the parcel sits. Section 119.04 also asks every buyer to give the City Engineer a description of the property within one month of acquiring title and to have the deed stamped as proof of registration.

Assessment appeals go to the county that assesses the parcel. Ask the Northampton County Assessment Division or the Lehigh County assessment office for the current annual appeal filing date, since each office sets its own.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection if I sell to a cash buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. The city states that all properties must be inspected prior to transfer of title, whatever the buyer's financing. Call the Housing Inspections Bureau within 10 days of offering the house, and plan for the report to go to the buyer.

faqs.q: How early should I schedule the Bethlehem sale inspection?
faqs.a: A month or more before the transfer date, and within 10 days of first offering the property for sale. Booking early leaves time to fix any housing, safety or fire items the inspector lists.

faqs.q: What happens if the inspection finds violations?
faqs.a: The report lists them and goes to the buyer as an addendum to the agreement of sale. The buyer must still obtain a certificate of occupancy, so many sellers repair the items first or negotiate who will.

faqs.q: Who bears the transfer tax on a Bethlehem sale?
faqs.a: The agreement of sale decides who pays, but state law makes both seller and buyer liable. The recorder of deeds collects the state tax and the local share at recording.

faqs.q: Which county records my Bethlehem deed?
faqs.a: Northampton County for most of the city. A parcel on the West Side is in Lehigh County and is recorded there. Check the county on your tax bill or assessment record before you schedule settlement.
